Why do we produce energy? To improve human lives—not to score political points, says @SecretaryWright. 

He argues that every energy policy should be judged by two standards: does it benefit people, and does the math back it up? 

Watch his remarks: piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Video

Does the 14th Amendment guarantee birthright citizenship to persons born in the US to parents without permanent immigration status? Join us for an insightful discussion with a group of scholars who will break down Trump v. Barbara, consider the recent Supreme Court oral argument, and explore the approaches the Court might take as it reaches a decision.
 
Featuring:
🔹 Dan Greenberg, Senior Legal Fellow, Cato Institute
🔹 @IlyaSomin, Professor of Law, George Mason University, and B. Kenneth Simon C

Many Americans think they understand today’s Supreme Court. But Sarah Isgur, host of the Advisory Opinions podcast, editor of @SCOTUSblog, and one of the savviest Court-watchers in the country, is here to tell you that’s wrong.

Join us for a conversation with @whignewtons about what may be the last constitutionally functioning branch of American government.

Register to attend and follow live: ow.ly/upv850Z1ix2

Virginia just banned "assault weapons." Within hours, it was hit with multiple lawsuits. 

One fights it under Virginia's own constitution. The other is designed to ultimately trigger a Supreme Court review. That's the whole point. They want SCOTUS to affirm that modern sporting rifles like the AR-15 are lawful for public ownership under the Second Amendment, says Cato’s @PGEddington. 

cato.org/blog/virginias-assa…

"That's how we create the most flourishing world possible. May the best ideas win." 

Cato Institute President and CEO Peter Goettler joins @spuri on the #RegulatingAI podcast to discuss the benefits of AI, the risks of overregulation, and why the market is the best regulator of all. 
piped.video/jZqUMzH26VY

When policy becomes “government-by-deal,” markets can’t rely on clear, predictable rules. 

Cato’s @DeHavenTad argues that Trump’s new personal financial disclosures highlight the risk of a president making investments while wielding vast discretion over firms—government ownership stakes, export approvals, mergers, and more.  
cato.org/blog/trumps-persona…

Energy Secretary, @SecretaryWright,
says hydrocarbons aren’t running out—we’ve barely scratched the surface. The biggest energy innovations in the coming decades will likely come from oil, gas, and coal.  ow.ly/TEKA50Z0owm

Video

President Trump’s tariffs were supposed to make “America Great.” Instead: farmers need bailouts, manufacturers are paying more, and prices are up. 

The experiment failed, as we warned, explains Cato’s @cpgrabow. It’s time for Republicans to go back to what works — free trade.  

ow.ly/KGPj50Z18fu

Cato’s Senior Legal Fellow Dan Greenberg warns of a dangerous precedent after Tina Peters' sentence reduction.

ow.ly/165k50Z1hT7

"How many more Stephanies have to die before DHS follows the law and prioritizes serious criminals?" Cato's @David_J_Bier testified before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on what went wrong — and how to fix it. 

Watch his full testimony: piped.video/UeRdruJGy2g

Video

What happens when an educator sees public school isn’t working for some kids? Sometimes, they build something new. Microschools are small, community-based learning models that are growing with school choice, explains Cato’s @ColleenHroncich.
 
ow.ly/xtB450Z17b4

Social Security is a major driver of federal borrowing, and the shortfall will only grow. The longer we wait to address the problem, the worse the outcome.

Video

Pennsylvania audited 210,905 voter registration forms tied to PennDOT. Result: 1 noncitizen was improperly sent and registered—he never voted and is no longer registered. Another real-world data point against claims of noncitizens voting en masse.

ow.ly/TvTT50Z0l0A

Utah Fits All helps families access educational options beyond their assigned public schools—but demand far outpaces funding. The constitution sets a floor for education, not a ceiling. Lawmakers should expand choice. 

ow.ly/Hrue50Z0kP2

Asylum legal entries are down 99.9%. Student visas, family visas, and H‑1B applications have cratered. 

@MrRBourne is joined by Cato’s @David_J_Bier to examine how President Trump’s executive actions have blocked more legal immigrants than illegal ones, and why the president’s stated support for legal immigration doesn’t match his policy record.
 
Listen to Cato Podcast on Spotify, Apple, and our website!
 
Spotify: ow.ly/6Lfh50Z0q8P 
Apple: ow.ly/aLy050Z0q8V 
Website: ow.ly/htgX50Z0q8Z

School choice is expanding fast—70+ programs across 30+ states. 

But passing a law isn’t enough: weak design creates waitlists, red tape, and lost opportunities. 

@ColleenHroncich outlines best practices to make educational freedom durable.
ow.ly/uM9250Z0aO5

More than 75 years after NATO’s founding, is a US withdrawal from Germany warranted? What are the likely consequences? Can the administration sustain a burden-shift to Europe? 

Join our panel of distinguished experts on transatlantic security to discuss these questions. 

Featuring: 
🔹 @LianaFix, Senior Fellow for Europe, Council on Foreign Relations
🔹 @jekavanagh, Senior Fellow & Director of Military Analysis at Defense Priorities
🔹 @JustinTLogan, Director of Defense and Foreign Policy Studies

Congress’s refusal to correct its past mistakes and legalize immigration has forced states and local governments to deal with the fallout of illegal immigration, says Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

Watch his testimony before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement: piped.video/UeRdruJGy2g

Video

Ayn Rand on monopolies: free markets—not regulators—are what keep monopolies in check. 

A genuinely free market, with low barriers to entry, makes it nearly impossible for any one player to dominate indefinitely.
